newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tsang confirms 4.7 pct Hong Kong growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: Tsang confirms 4.7 pct Hong Kong growth forecast.

text.p: Financial Secretary Donald Tsang on Friday confirmed Hong Kong's half yearly economic report for 1996 would officially forecast 4.7 percent economic growth for the current financial year.
"Our economists have just finished their computer run and told me last night it was 4.7 percent," Tsang told Reuters. "I did forecast 5.0, but 4.7 is on the trend line of 5.0," he said.
Tsang said that in the first two quarters, external trade was "not brilliant at all" and a bit less than he thought.
But this was not unique to Hong Kong. "In the entire East Asia economies, every finance minister has been reducing their forecasts because of that. For whatever reason, I am not too sure."
Tsang speculated the lacklustre external trade position may have been a result of currency movements.
"But to me, it is still looking pretty good," he said.
Hong Kong's economic report is due around 0730 GMT.
